Generate Hexagonal Surveillance Grid

Source: R/grids.R
d4h_hex_grid.Rd

Creates an operative hexagonal surveillance grid with unique alphanumeric identifiers over an Area of Interest (AOI).

Usage

d4h_hex_grid(aoi, cell_size = 50, clip_to_footprint = TRUE)

Arguments

aoi

SpatRaster, SpatVector, sf, or character path defining the spatial bounds or mosaic.

cell_size

Numeric. Hexagon diameter in meters (default: 50).

clip_to_footprint

Logical. If TRUE (default), restricts grid cells strictly to the valid non-NA flight footprint of the input raster or polygon boundaries.

Value

A SpatVector containing the hexagonal grid polygons with unique IDs.

Details

Hexagonal spatial partitions minimize perimeter-to-area ratio and provide equidistant neighborhood connectivity: $$A_{\text{hex}} = \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} r^2$$ Ideal for vector control teams, larviciding deployments, and spatial health sampling. By default, cells are clipped strictly to the valid non-NA flight footprint of the raster or polygon boundaries (clip_to_footprint = TRUE) to prevent artificial bounding-box grid padding outside the surveyed area.

References

Carr, D. B., Olsen, A. R., & White, D. (1992). Hexagon mosaic maps for display of univariate and bivariate data. Cartography and Geographic Information Systems, 19(4), 228-236. doi:10.1559/152304092783721231

Examples

# \donttest{
if (interactive()) {
  library(drones4health)
  library(terra)

  # Define Area of Interest raster
  aoi_file <- system.file("extdata", "ortho_rgb.tif", package = "drones4health")

  # Create hexagonal grid cells with 50-meter diameter clipped to flight footprint
  hex_grid <- d4h_hex_grid(aoi = aoi_file, cell_size = 50, clip_to_footprint = TRUE)
  plot(hex_grid)
}
# }
